## 1. AO Standards — What Makes Top-1% vs Generic

### 1.1 The non-negotiable AO scan

Admissions officers spend **~2-3 minutes** on the entire activities list before reading essays (Oriel: "Ivy League AOs have limited time per application and scan the activities list before reading essays"). The list is therefore **not a résumé dump** — it is the first evidence of judgment.

Four qualities AOs are explicitly hunting (Crimson survey of former AOs on thousands of admits):

> **Leadership, impact, initiative, and ambition** — Crimson Education, synth. of former AO interviews: "AOs scrutinize the Activities List to gain deeper understanding of interests, commitments, contributions outside classroom."

> **"Extracurricular activities can be a great opportunity to see how an applicant has self-directed their passions and interests. There are only so many hours in the day so seeing how a student has involved themselves outside the academic arena is a great way of understanding their potential fit for a university campus."** — Jorge Delgado, Associate Director of International Admissions, Brandeis (quoted in College Essay Guy)

> **"The Common App activities section is the most misunderstood part of your application — partly because 150 characters is so tight it feels like there's no room for anything real."** — Marina Hovhannisyan, HYE Tutors (8 years, 500+ apps reviewed): "Include (a) your specific contribution, (b) a measurable outcome or impact, and (c) what changed because of your involvement."

> **"Do not use it to pad the application with filler. Admissions readers can tell the difference."** — CollegeAdvisor / Shemmassian on blank slots vs padding.

### 1.2 Top-1% markers (synthesis across all sources)

| Marker | Generic version | Top-1% version |
|---|---|---|
| **Owns the verb** | "Helped with various projects" / "Participated" / "Member" | First word is a strong, specific verb: Built, Engineered, Led, Authored, Validated, Ran, Recovered |
| **Quantifies on entry** | "Raised a significant amount" / "Taught many kids" | "Raised ₹25,000+; delivered kits to children in rural villages" — number + scope + recipient |
| **Separates role from work** | Repeats Position box: "As president I led the club" | Position box already says "Founder & President" → description starts with what changed |
| **Impact > duties** | "Responsible for organizing meetings" | "Organized 12 service events for 80+ members; grew chapter 15→40" |
| **Selectivity signal** | "Published a paper" | "Peer-reviewed Q1 (Borsa Istanbul Review) — Accepted after peer review; Corresponding author" or "1 of 5 selected out of 100" |
| **Tiering** | 10 equal slots | Spike at top: 1-4 reinforce one intellectual story; 5-10 show breadth/humility; no filler at bottom |
| **Voice** | Corporate/puffed ("maximized synergies") | Plain, defensible verbs a 17-year-old would actually own under questioning |

> **"If you can cut a word and the meaning stays the same, cut it. Specificity is your fingerprint — AI can't fake it authentically."** — HYE Tutors mentor insight.

> **"A description that opens with measurable impact stands out immediately, while one that merely restates a title blends into the page."** — Oriel Admissions.

### 1.3 Failed Simulation Effect (Shemmassian / Cal Newport)

> **"Accomplishments that are hard to explain can be much more impressive than accomplishments that are simply hard to do."** — Dr. Cal Newport, via Shemmassian.

Application: do not hide the *hard-to-explain* part behind generic duties. For Aditya, the hard-to-explain signals are not "did research" but:

- "Validated 9/9 stylized facts via jump-filtered ARCH LM (Andersen et al.) — believed only undergrad ABM to do so"
- "γ*=1.5625 via Lewbel IV + SMM cross-validation across empirical + simulated markets"
- "86.7% top-1 vs 13.3% baseline (15-scenario seeded harness)"

These survive because they are *falsifiable specifics*, not adjectives.

### 1.4 Tier framework (AdmissionSight, synthesis of AO practice)

- **Tier 1 — Rare distinction:** national/international, hard to replicate (e.g., Q1 peer-reviewed publication as corresponding author, national team, Regeneron ISEF award).
- **Tier 2 — High leadership / state+ recognition:** Founder of active org with measurable users (ATLAS used in production; Daedalus used by STEM Racing team; Future Lab 150-stock market); state-level competition wins.
- **Tier 3 — Sustained participation with concrete contribution:** Volunteer teaching 50+ children with adapted pedagogy; crowdfunding with logistics; club leadership that kept members returning.
- **Tier 4 — General membership:** "Participant," "attended meetings." Should never occupy limited slots unless it adds a distinct human dimension — and even then must be rewritten away from Tier-4 phrasing.

**Relevance:** Aditya's list is unusually Tier-1/2 heavy (papers + production platforms). The danger is *not* weakness but **credibility collapse** if four entries read identically technical. Ordering + role clarity + varied verbs are the anti-collapse tools.

## 2. The 150-Character Formula

### 2.1 Canonical build (GradGPT / CollegeHound / Oriel — convergent)

```
Verb + Specific What + Scale/Frequency + Outcome
```

Expanded checklist per entry (all sources agree):

1. **Verb** — first word, no "I" (saves 2-3 chars; reader knows it's you).
2. **Specific what** — not the category, but the mechanism/object: not "did research" but "Built 22-market Lewbel IV threshold model" or "Engineered LangGraph SRE pipeline."
3. **Scale** — numerals always: "22 markets," "10,200 Monte Carlo sims," "50+ children," "35% token reduction," "4.57 days/yr, R²=0.83, p=0.0003."
4. **Outcome / what exists because of you** — validation, adoption, or human change: "Confirmed 14/22 markets," "86.7% top-1 vs 13.3% baseline," "Used by CS grad / STEM Racing team for real trade-offs," "Entered Oxford Saïd Climate Challenge."

### 2.2 Character economics (Common App official PDF 2025.06.25)

- **Position/Leadership:** 50 chars (include selectivity here if needed: "Lead Researcher (Corresponding Author)")
- **Organization:** 100 chars (use to carry journal/platform name so description doesn't waste them: "Borsa Istanbul Review (Q1)" / "QUANT360 / ATLAS Platform")
- **Description:** 150 chars — spaces + punctuation count. Fragments expected. Semicolons > periods (saves chars, packs clauses).

**Free character buys** (GradGPT, CollegeHound, Shemmassian — verbatim advice):

- Drop "I" / "my" / articles "a/an/the" where meaning holds
- Numerals: "12" not "twelve"; "3x/week" not "three times per week"
- "&" and ";" instead of "and" / full sentences
- Abbreviate only if an outsider parses it: "HS," "natl," "dept," "w/" — never internal acronyms
- Never repeat Position or Organization text inside description

**Example of compression progression (GradGPT):**

> Draft 1 (50c): "Member of debate team, participated in tournaments"
> Draft 2 (96c): "Competed in public forum debate tournaments; researched cases and practiced with the team weekly"
> Draft 3 (150c): "Prepped 2 case files/week; competed in 12 PF tournaments, reached state octofinals; ran drills for 6 novices who all broke at their first varsity meet"

Same activity, 3x the information — because scale + outcome were added, not adjectives.

### 2.3 MIT-specific note

MIT form asks for **only four activities** ("There is only enough space to list four things — please choose the four that mean the most to you" — MIT Admissions, Essays/Activities/Academics). Each has limited space but is read alongside the four 100-200-word essays. Strategy: the 150-char MIT entry must *not* duplicate the essay's story — it anchors the factual claim the essay then reflects on (see §8).

## 3. Verb Bank — Tiered by Function

Derived from College Essay Guy "Epic List of Activities List Verbs," plus Shemmassian/AdmissionSight/GradGPT verb lists. Organized for Aditya's profile to avoid "helped/participated/assisted" repetition across 19→10 and MIT 4.

### 3.1 Research & Analysis (use sparingly — one technical verb per entry max)

Designed, Engineered, Built, Validated, Recovered, Corroborated, Estimated, Tested, Derived, Proved, Quantified, Modeled, Simulated, Integrated, Estimated (γ*), Ran (10,200 sims), Implemented (GARCH/DCC-GARCH/Double ML)

**Upgrade ladder:**
- Weak: "researched," "studied," "analyzed"
- Strong: "Designed GASI index across 22 markets via Lewbel IV" / "Validated 9/9 stylized facts via jump-filtered ARCH LM"
- Peak: add falsification — "Confirmed in 14/22 markets via synthetic-control falsification"

### 3.2 Building & Shipping

Built, Engineered, Shipped, Launched, Architected, Deployed, Implemented, Optimized, Vectorized, Integrated (GBIF/MODIS/NOAA/FAOSTAT), Automated (Playwright), Reduced (35% tokens), Achieved (86.7% vs 13.3%)

### 3.3 Leadership & Scale (not titles)

Founded, Co-founded, Led, Grew (15→40), Recruited (25-30 members), Designed (13-week curriculum), Ran, Hosted, Sustained, Coordinated

**Caution from College Essay Guy — "Corporate" verbs to avoid unless perfectly earned:**
> allocated, apprised, arbitrated, audited, augmented, dispatched, executed, expedited, maximized, presided, standardized, substantiated, yielded — "Proceed with caution. Unless it's the one and only word that perfectly captures what you did, avoid."

### 3.4 Teaching & Service (human impact)

Taught, Adapted (lessons weekly until material stuck), Raised (₹25,000+), Delivered (kits/clothing/footwear), Reached (50+ children), Mentored

### 3.5 Allowed tense rule (all sources converge)

- Still doing → **present tense**: "Lead," "Run," "Teach"
- Finished → **past tense**: "Built," "Authored," "Validated"
- Use consistently per entry; fragments okay: "Led 30-member club; organized weekly meetings…"

**Variety rule (College Essay Guy 10 Tips #1):** Never open two entries with the same verb. If "Built" opens ATLAS, open Glassbox with "Engineered" and PhenoSync with "Integrated" or "Recovered."

## 4. Quantification Rules

> **"Numbers make your accomplishments specific and measurable. They help admissions officers see the scope of your work and the results you achieved."** — AdmissionSight

> **"Instead of 'Raised money for children in Africa,' try 'Raised $3,000 to provide three uniforms and scholarships for students attending the Joseph Waweru Home School in Kenya.'"** — College Essay Guy

### 4.1 What to quantify (apply to every Aditya entry)

| Domain | Quantities that earn characters |
|---|---|
| Research | N markets / N gameweeks / simulations (22 markets, 380 gameweeks, 10,200 sims); threshold value + CI (γ*=1.5625, CI [1.14,2.50]); test stat (t=-57.20); validation rate (14/22, 9/9, 105/105 OOS); paper length/status (peer-reviewed Q1, under review, SSRN, 4,982-word) |
| Platforms | Modules (8 modules, 9 features), tech stack compression (Next.js/FastAPI/Postgres/Three.js into one phrase only where needed), users ("Used by CS grad for real analysis" / "Team relies on it for trade-off decisions"), optimization metric (35% token reduction; 86.7% vs 13.3%) |
| Clubs / Leadership | Members (25-30), weeks (13-week curriculum), industries (15), stocks (150), companies engine (OU mean-reversion) — pick 1-2 per entry max |
| Service | Children (50+), amount (₹25,000+), kits type, cadence (weekly adapted lessons) |
| Time | Hours/week + weeks/year must be honest (see §4.2) |

### 4.2 Hours/weeks honesty rule (CollegeVine + Common App official)

> **"You should never lie on your college applications. It’s okay that [hours] is an estimate as long as you’re being honest. Rounding to an hour if it sometimes only meets for 55 minutes is understandable. Calculating an hour when you likely only spend 30 minutes is not honest."** — CollegeVine, 5 Successful Entries.

> **"Count not just time spent doing an activity, but also time spent preparing and traveling."** — Shemmassian.

For Aditya: self-directed research + building has fuzzy hours. Best practice is to **average over weeks the activity actually ran** (Shemmassian: fall sport 12 hrs × 14 wks = 12 & 14, never 3 & 52). Summer internship (MalkansView ~140 hrs over ~12 wks) → mark as Summer, calculate accordingly. Push inflated padding into Additional Information transparency instead.

### 4.3 When numbers hurt

- Never invent precision the fact sheet cannot defend (e.g., "₹25,000+" is correct per fact sheet; "₹25,437" is not).
- If outcome is not yet accepted, name status truthfully: "Peer-reviewed Q1, accepted" (GASI) vs "Under review at J. Sports Econ (Q1)" (BOG) — do not upgrade.
- One quantified claim per entry beats three vague ones. Shemmassian: "Focus on quantifiable and significant impact — numbers that jump out and demand attention."

## 5. Before / After Examples — 15 Peak Rewrites (verbatim structure models)

All "After" entries are built to fit 150 chars and to follow Verb + Specific What + Scale + Outcome. Each lists character length where the source does. Sources tagged.

### General Member → Leader with outcome

> **Before:** "I was a member of Model UN and attended meetings and conferences." → **After:** `Researched and drafted policy positions for 3 conferences; won Best Delegate at regional competition as a junior (113 chars)` — CollegeHound

> **Before:** "As president, I ran meetings and planned activities for our chapter." → **After:** `Grew chapter from 15 to 40 members; launched peer tutoring program serving 60 students weekly across 5 subjects (110 chars)` — CollegeHound

### Research: vague → falsifiable

> **Before:** "I conduct research in the biology lab at the local university under a professor." → **After:** `Co-authored paper on CRISPR gene editing (submitted to J. Molecular Bio); presented at 2 natl conferences` — Oriel

> **Before:** "Studied microplastic pollution in local waterways. Presented findings at regional science fair, won 2nd place." → **Model:** Add method: `Designed & ran 6-mo water quality study of 3 streams; presented findings to town council (81 chars + add'l info)` — College Essay Mentor (Add Info method)

### Volunteering: generic → scaled

> **Before:** "I volunteered at a food bank and helped sort donations." → **After:** `Sorted and distributed 2,000+ lbs of food monthly; trained 15 new volunteers; created inventory tracking system (111 chars)` — CollegeHound

> **Before:** "Tutored students." → **After:** `Tutored 15 middle schoolers in math, improving grades by 20%` (quantified outcome) — AdmissionSight + Dewey Smart pattern

### Work: under-sold → responsibility-forward

> **Before:** "I worked as a tutor helping kids with their homework." → **After:** `Managed 8-table section during peak hours; trained 4 new hires; promoted to shift lead after 6 months (100 chars)` — CollegeHound (retail mapping: replace tables with tutees/jobs)

> **Before:** "Interned at XYZ Company; assisted with marketing campaigns and social media management." → **After:** Add real responsibility: `Analyzed data for 200+ patient records; co-authored research abstract` (CollegeAdvisor research intern) — same principle for Aditya's quant internship

### Arts / Athletics: participation → measurable craft

> **Before:** "I played on the varsity basketball team for two years and we had a great season." → **After:** `Started 48 games over 2 seasons; averaged 12 pts/game; led team in assists and was named All-Conference honorable mention (120 chars)` — CollegeHound

> **Before:** "Participated in beach cleanups..." → **After:** `Pack and hand out 120 grocery boxes every Saturday; built Spanish-language signup flyer that grew families served by 30% (129 chars)` — GradGPT

### Aditya-mapping rewrites (apply formula to actual activities — ready patterns)

> **Crowdfunding (current 150c: "Raised ₹25,000+; delivered study kits, clothing & footwear to underprivileged rural children; led outreach & logistics" — 105 chars)** → Peak tightness keeps it but adds verification: `Raised ₹25,000+ via crowdfunding; delivered study kits, clothing & footwear to rural children; coordinated outreach & logistics` — holds 150 budget for position/org specificity

> **Teaching (current: "Taught foundational math & English to 50+ underprivileged rural children; adapted lessons weekly until the material actually stuck" — 112 chars)** → Keep human mechanism, add cadence: `Taught foundational math & English to 50+ rural children; adapted lessons weekly until material stuck; returned weekly` — demonstrates persistence per §1.2

> **MalkansView (current: "Interned at quant firm MalkansView; researched company fundamentals & applied analytical frameworks to real market data over 140 hours" — 132 chars)** → Strong but move hours to Hours field; spend chars on judgment: `Interned at stock research firm MalkansView; analyzed company fundamentals via analytical frameworks on live market data; saw research → investment decisions` — still within 150

### High-credibility research entry (CollegeVine 5 Successful Entries — style to emulate)

> ` Provided homework and study help to underprivileged kids. I studied with one girl until her Cs became As. I love being the "go-to" mentor. ` — NYC Cares Volunteer, 2 hrs/wk × 16 wks/yr (CollegeVine: "quantifies service + exhibits emotional investment; names charity to signal initiative")

Lesson for Aditya: even the most technical entries benefit from **one human clause** where appropriate — e.g., for teaching/service entries keep one; for Q1 papers keep fully technical.

### Leadership selectives (College Essay Guy + CollegeVine)

> ` 1 of 2 student leaders elected by peers to represent class of 450 ` — selectivity signal (College Essay Guy)

> ` 9 seniors are chosen as leaders of junior retreat. We meet weekly to critique speeches and mediate small-group discussion. ` — Retreat Leader (CollegeVine)

Lesson: where selectivity is real (Q1 peer review, corresponding author, platform used in production), state it once, plainly: "Corresponding author, peer-reviewed Q1" not "prestigious."

### Service / niche standout (GradGPT — memorable because rare)

> `Moderate daily posts on a 40,000-member aquarium forum; wrote beginner tank-cycling guide pinned since 2024, answer 20+ questions/week (141 chars)` — GradGPT: "A reader sees 40 debate captains a day and one aquarium forum moderator a season."

Lesson: NEXUS / ATLAS / Glassbox niche depth beats generic breadth — but must be *explained* in plain language, not jargon-stacked.

### Common App official: edited vs original

> **Original (256 chars):** "For two years I volunteered at my local animal shelter. I helped out where needed, but mainly walked dogs and monitored the front desk. Last year I was asked to take on more responsibility and have been volunteering as the receptionist during weekends." → **Edited (141 chars):** "Volunteer at local animal shelter walking dogs and running front desk. Given more responsibility last year and now volunteer as receptionist." — Common App official PDF, 2025.06.25. Rule demonstrated: remove time already captured in hours/weeks fields.

## 6. Pitfalls — What Wastes the 150 and Credibility

Synthesized from CollegeHound Common Mistakes, GradGPT Mistakes, Shemmassian, College Essay Guy 10 Tips, Common App official.

1. **Repeating Position/Org in description.** If Position = "Researcher" and Org = "Borsa Istanbul Review (Q1)," do not open with "Researched investor attention at Borsa Istanbul Review." — College Essay Guy #4.

2. **"I / my" and full sentences.** Drop pronouns; fragments expected. Saves 2-3 chars per clause and reads as resume signal — all sources converge.

3. **Weak verbs: helped / participated / assisted / was responsible for.** Shemmassian #4: use `implemented, led, founded, tutored, established, managed, launched`. College Essay Guy: "helped" describes attendance.

4. **Same verb ten times.** If "Built" opens three entries, AOs read padding — GradGPT.

5. **Duty list without result.** "Attended weekly meetings" in four entries = breadth without depth — AdmissionSight: "vary focus: leadership in one, results in another."

6. **Acronym soup / TITLE CASE shouting.** "VP of SNHS, ran BOB prep for MSA" means nothing outside building — GradGPT. Use normal capitalization always.

7. **Extreme language.** "to end poverty in the world" → "to fight global poverty" — College Essay Guy #9. For Aditya: avoid "revolutionary," "groundbreaking," "world's first" unless literally defensible (e.g., "believed only undergrad ABM achieving 9/9 validation" is hedged correctly).

8. **Padding empty slots.** "An empty slot costs nothing. A 9th-grade club you attended twice dilutes entries above it." — GradGPT. Aditya has 19 raw entries; must compress to 10 Common App + 4 MIT — leaving slots blank is strategic, not weak.

9. **AI-corporate verb inflation.** See §3.3 caution list — reads as ghostwritten if every verb is "synergized/leveraged."

10. **Method stacking.** One technical mechanism per entry: "Lewbel IV" OR "GARCH/DCC-GARCH" — not both in 150 chars. Supplement-master-material guardrail: "one technical object per short essay" applies equally to activity lines.

11. **Inconsistency as signal of padding:** Hours that imply 45 hrs/week of activities alongside school → AO quietly checks total (GradGPT). Keep averages honest.

## 7. MIT vs Common App — What Changes

| Dimension | Common App (10 activities, 150c each) | MIT (4 activities, short form) | Common App Additional Information (new 300-word box, 2025-26) / UC 350c |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Slots** | 10; order = importance to you (Common App instruction). First 4 get most attention. | 4 only: "please choose the four that mean the most to you" (MIT Admissions). Not a resume — pick functions, not titles. Master doc recommends: GASI research / ATLAS or Glassbox / Quant Finance Club-Future Lab / rural teaching or goalkeeping — four different functions. | 300 words first-year (down from 650); transfers 1500 chars. Separate 250-word Challenges & Circumstances box for hardship transcript impact — do not conflate. |
| **Fields** | Activity Type dropdown (30 cats) + 50c Position + 100c Organization + 150c Description + grade/hours/weeks/continue | MIT form: "use our form, not a resume" — shorter structured entries, then essays do heavy lifting | Free-text prose; not bullet-resume repetition. Use for overflow methodology, academic context, or unusual circumstance only. |
| **Description goal** | Four-part: verb + what + scale + outcome (see §2.1) | Same tightness, but AO reads it *with* essays: entry should tee up essay's reflection, not repeat it. | "Extended fact, not second personal statement." Narrative arc / reflection belongs in 100-200-word MIT essays or 250-word Stanford/Princeton essays, not here. |
| **How to handle long research** | Keep 150c factual; add "(see Add'l Info)" at end of description, expand in Add Info with why + method + result sentence (College Essay Mentor pattern). | Put one lab/paper per MIT slot max; use essay #1-3 to unpack the question behind it (MIT "what led you" / "problems to tackle"). | Add Info example for research: water-study entry + 80-hr provenance paragraph (see §7.1). For Aditya, GASI/NEXUS/ATLAS each would need the Add Info paragraph if compressed. |
| **Common mistake** | Repeating position/org; padding to 10; listing middle-school | Trying to list 10 anyway; using resume formatting | Dumping every activity's overflow into 300 words ("crowded box sometimes hurts" — Essay Mentor) or linking external portfolio instead of expanding inline |

### 7.1 Three legitimate uses of Additional Information (Essay Mentor taxonomy)

1. **Activity that needs more room than 150 chars allows** — methodology, phases, self-directed provenance. Pattern:
   - Activity list: `Designed & ran 6-mo water quality study of 3 local streams; presented findings to town council (see Add'l Info)`
   - Add Info: 3-5 sentences: origin, method (pH/nitrate/turbidity weekly, database), finding (nitrate spikes lined to fertilizer after rain), outcome (council considering buffer zone), hours provenance. Factual, no story arc.

   *For Aditya, this maps to:*
   - GASI: "Designed Global Attention Saturation Index across 22 markets via Lewbel IV; γ*=1.5625, CI [1.14,2.50]; Silence Signature 14/22; peer-reviewed Q1 (see Add'l Info)" → Add Info expands Hansen CIs, Driscoll-Kraay SEs, synthetic-control falsification in ~45 words.
   - ATLAS: "Built QUANT360 quant platform (8 modules: GARCH/DCC-GARCH, Double ML, HRP); free data only; used by CS grad in production" → Add Info expands two engines not list.

2. **Academic context that would otherwise look strange** — scheduling conflict, choice between two same-period courses, curriculum gap. ~50 words, factual. Example: chose AP Chem same period as AP Bio because it builds on materials research; continuing bio independently via community college.

3. **Unusual circumstance that needs a sentence, not an essay** — work/family obligation that explains why EC list is shorter. One sentence + skill framing (manage kitchen schedule, train staff, handle Friday rush) rather than excuse.

**Do NOT put in Add Info:** second personal statement, repeated resume, defense of a single B, links/portfolios (readers won't click), excuse for not liking a teacher — Scholarships360 + Essay Mentor converge.

## 8. Extended Descriptions — 300-Word / MIT-Essay Adjacent Rules

> The task prompt asks for "600-char details" — this vault treats that as the **MIT long essay adjacency (100-200 words per essay) + Common App Additional Information (300 words)** and **UC 350-char** extended description. Common App Activities themselves remain 150 chars; the extension box changed 2025-26 to 300 words. All character counts include spaces/punctuation.

### 8.1 Structure for any 300-word extension

1. **One sentence — why the work started** (real observation, not "passion for finance").
2. **Two sentences — method, but at mechanism level** (what you separated/tested, not inventory of libraries).
3. **One sentence — result / validation against expectation.**
4. **One sentence — what another person did with it or what changes with more time.**

> Test per supplement-master-material §9: read aloud; must sound like one person thinking, not a consultant arranging virtues. Contain at least one sentence that could *only* belong to Aditya (specific object/question/result).

### 8.2 MIT 100-200-word essay adjacency

From MIT's own framing of the four 100-200-word essays + 40-50-word shorts (supplement-master-material §5): the activity list should **not** retell the essay arc. Examples:

- **If essay covers GASI Silence Signature** (intellectual curiosity), the activity entry stays factual: "Corresponding author, Borsa Istanbul Review (Q1); Lewbel IV threshold γ*=1.5625; 14/22 markets validated." Essay adds the moment you treated non-moving output as suspicious vs broken.
- **If essay covers "different educational journey"** via NTK-from-A-levels derivation, the activity entry for NTK paper is spare: "Authored 15-pp NTK exposition from Further Maths matrices/eigenvalues/ODEs; 2-neuron worked example" — essay carries the curriculum-you-built reflection.

### 8.3 Real-user proof (Lane B of master doc)

> "Do not treat 'used in production' as a trophy. Show what the user needed, what changed because of feedback, or what responsibility real use created." — supplement-master-material Lane B guardrail.

Therefore extension must include one of:

- Graduate user querying an assumption in ATLAS not visible to builder.
- STEM Racing teammate needing a trade-off decision (not dashboard) from Daedalus.
- Future Lab member's decision inside 150-stock market — not just market existence.

Retrieve one exact interaction before drafting final extended text.

| 1 MalkansView | Yes (keep but light) | Keep low in order or merge hours | Professional supervised contrast to self-directed work |
| 4 Crowdfunding + 5 Teaching | Keep both but write distinctly (§1.4 variety): 4 = logistics, 5 = pedagogy adaptation | Keep | Service Tier 3 — human range; AOs weight caregiving/translation style plain verbs (GradGPT) |
| 2 Sports Analysis Hub + 3/11 IAYP | Hub Yes; IAYP merge into one entry (Bronze + Silver progression: 26-wk quant project) | Merge | Hub shows "presence not title" leadership; IAYP cannot remain two rows |

Net: 10 Common App slots can carry GASI, BOG, NEXUS, PhenoSync(m), ATLAS, Glassbox, Daedalus, Quant Finance Club, Teaching, Crowdfunding/Sports Hub (choose human slot) — with MalkansView/HUB/IAYP rotating into 10th or Add Info. MIT 4 then selects from among these per master doc: GASI / ATLAS-or-Glassbox / Quant Finance Club / Teaching-or-Goalkeeping.

### 9.3 Ordering principle (all sources: importance to you, not chronology)

Recommended Common App order (impact-first, per §1.2 + §7 table):

1. Spike that defines story (GASI for investor-attention threshold) — even though title "Researcher, Independent" sounds humble vs "Founder"
2. Second angle on same spike (NEXUS simulator corroboration — shows method expansion)
3. Production credibility (ATLAS or Glassbox — shows building for others)
4. Leadership infrastructure (Quant Finance Club / Future Lab)
5. Remaining Tier-1 research (BOG under review)
6. Climate quantitative pipeline (PhenoSync merged)
7. Daedalus real-tool use
8. MalkansView supervised professional work
9. Service — teaching
10. Service/community — crowdfunding or Sports Hub (human texture)

GradGPT ordering axiom: **promotion rule when tied** — promote whichever adds a dimension slot 1 didn't show (e.g., after two research slots, next is paid work / caregiving).
